title: Provider rebuild source accounting

sourcePack.authority: Unchanged original mapping pack; rows are mappings/proposals, not accepted implementation dispositions.

implementationEvidenceSnapshot.recordedAcceptanceSummary: Historical committed receipt; regenerate its producer for the current checkout. Current externally retained results and exact inputs are summarized in the verification handoff.
implementationEvidenceSnapshot.releaseState: Full conversion/research/readiness obligations remain enforced; no release or source disposition inferred.
implementationEvidenceSnapshot.rawArtifactsPolicy: External logs, screenshots, traces and saves; no raw artifacts committed.

playRequirements.title: Default provider campaign
playRequirements.behaviour: Play and Continue open a management campaign. Training, Lab and the retained SP game are separate experiences.

playRequirements.title: Campaign authority boundary
playRequirements.behaviour: Separate player actions, scenario authorship and evaluation at the shared dispatcher, including nested customer commands.

playRequirements.title: Purchased starting estate
playRequirements.behaviour: Start with one home market, a finite team and purchasable capability. Canonical resource IDs may exist as dormant internal blueprints.

playRequirements.title: One explicit clock
playRequirements.behaviour: Retain integer simulation minutes and 60-minute billing periods. Initial pacing is 1 simulation minute per 2 real seconds at 1x.

playRequirements.title: Atomic quotes and purchases
playRequirements.behaviour: A pure quote explains upfront cost, recurring commitments, lead time, labour, capacity and consequences. Commit recalculates against the current revision.

playRequirements.title: One provider treasury
playRequirements.behaviour: All customers share one parent cash balance, credit agreement and provider team. Customer views are attributed subledgers.

playRequirements.title: Funding and insolvency
playRequirements.behaviour: Enforce upfront affordability and authored credit limits, and model unpaid posted obligations as visible arrears/default states.

playRequirements.title: Separate success states
playRequirements.behaviour: Tutorial, service readiness, contract delivery, operating profit, progression and mission victory use distinct state and labels.

playRequirements.title: Versioned experience and saves
playRequirements.behaviour: Add a versioned experience discriminator without repurposing guided/assessed/sandbox or the existing SOC_CAMPAIGN training scheduler.

playRequirements.title: Autonomous customer work
playRequirements.behaviour: Seeded campaign demand produces customer jobs through the authoritative simulation and drives visible service flows.

playRequirements.title: Period-history settlement
playRequirements.behaviour: Accumulate service, usage and obligation history throughout the period and settle each contract from that history.

playRequirements.title: Duration-bearing ordinary calls
playRequirements.behaviour: Ordinary calls occupy the appropriate capacity over a connected phase; probes are separate.

playRequirements.title: Live media consequences
playRequirements.behaviour: Active ordinary calls and meetings continuously evaluate their effective media path and supported fallback.

playRequirements.title: Admission and reservations
playRequirements.behaviour: Use consistent admission, reservation and exactly-once release for constrained sessions, recording, meetings, people and processors.

playRequirements.title: Scarce provider labour
playRequirements.behaviour: Deployment, migration, investigation, repair and bulk administration consume finite provider work capacity.

playRequirements.title: Two viable opening plans
playRequirements.behaviour: Author at least two sustainable opening solutions with different cost, lead time, margin, resilience or flexibility.

playRequirements.title: Upstream game frame
playRequirements.behaviour: Reuse upstream hierarchy and visual language: full-screen world, compact HUD, goals/deals/incidents navigation and contextual inspector.

playRequirements.title: Playable service map
playRequirements.behaviour: Project actual purchased suppliers, tenants, sites, platforms, integrations and workload paths into a selectable map.

playRequirements.title: Contextual decision cards
playRequirements.behaviour: Expose a few relevant verbs for the selected scope, using supported choices and readable consequences.

playRequirements.title: Stable UI during ticks
playRequirements.behaviour: Retain DOM identity or use keyed updates so simulation updates do not reset user work.

playRequirements.title: Accessible equivalent controls
playRequirements.behaviour: Provide keyboard and screen-reader operation alongside the canvas, plus touch and reduced-motion support.

playRequirements.title: Readable consequences
playRequirements.behaviour: Show service results, customer impact, reservations, progress and earned money at the action location and in a short event feed.

playRequirements.title: Six-step coaching
playRequirements.behaviour: Guide actual play using state-based goals and highlights; show alternatives instead of prescribing every field.

playRequirements.title: Optional diagnosis
playRequirements.behaviour: Translate traces and dependencies into service explanations; keep raw records behind an advanced diagnostics view.

playRequirements.title: Consequential incidents
playRequirements.behaviour: Seed incidents from owned dependencies and scenario risk with meaningful recovery or mitigation choices.

playRequirements.title: Renewal, price and customer choice
playRequirements.behaviour: Customers consider authored service needs, price, delivered outcomes and switching friction.

playRequirements.title: Commercial progression
playRequirements.behaviour: Success unlocks new contracts, capabilities, supplier terms, markets or useful automation.

playRequirements.title: Automation with tradeoffs
playRequirements.behaviour: Let mastered work become templates, scoped policy and scheduled operations that consume appropriate capacity and cost.

playRequirements.title: Portfolio continuity
playRequirements.behaviour: All active customers advance on one provider clock regardless of which customer is selected.

playRequirements.title: Workload substitution
playRequirements.behaviour: Model WhatsApp/Messenger, workplace chat/Slack and video as eligible workload alternatives and competing propositions.

playRequirements.title: Finance and operating report
playRequirements.behaviour: Present period revenue, usage, wholesale costs, payroll, credits, commitments and net operating result separately.

playRequirements.title: SMB campaign
playRequirements.behaviour: A complete SMB mission makes capital, price, delivery speed and a small workforce matter.

playRequirements.title: Enterprise campaign
playRequirements.behaviour: A complete enterprise mission covers mixed estate migration and continuity with rooms/interoperability and contact-centre work.

playRequirements.title: Government campaign
playRequirements.behaviour: A complete government mission imposes authored processing, storage, retention, administration/support and delegated-access constraints.

playRequirements.title: Defence campaign
playRequirements.behaviour: A complete defence mission requires declared local operation, dependency survival and controlled reconnection.

playRequirements.title: Microsoft family pathways
playRequirements.behaviour: Connect the existing six Microsoft-oriented family profiles to playable offers, dependencies and customer outcomes.

playRequirements.title: Cisco family pathways
playRequirements.behaviour: Connect the existing eight Cisco-oriented profiles to playable cloud, dedicated/premises, CC, CPaaS, device, provider, government and local-speech choices.

playRequirements.title: Channel and partner roles
playRequirements.behaviour: Supplier, carrier/SP, distributor, reseller, MSP, integrator, BPO and customer roles change authority, cost, workload or commercial access.

playRequirements.title: Third-party ecosystem
playRequirements.behaviour: Make compatibility, operating effort and specialist capabilities determine useful third-party purchases.

playRequirements.title: CC people and quality
playRequirements.behaviour: Keep licences, people, skills, schedules, presence and digital concurrency independent. Preserve current costed coaching and quality receipts.

playRequirements.title: Meetings, rooms and video
playRequirements.behaviour: Room/calendar/identity/device/interop/codec dependencies affect joining and supported quality.

playRequirements.title: Information and transcription
playRequirements.behaviour: Capture, processing, quality/language, storage, access, retention and locality are separate obligations.

playRequirements.title: CPaaS and digital journeys
playRequirements.behaviour: Offer purchasable workflows with channel accounts, rate limits, per-use cost, retry behaviour and human handoff.

playRequirements.title: On-premises and physical dependencies
playRequirements.behaviour: Retain real transport, local platforms, power, hardware and survivability when they change UC outcomes.

playRequirements.title: Pure rendering and shared dispatch
playRequirements.behaviour: UI, worker, automation and MCP use the same validated rules; rendering is a read-only projection.

playRequirements.title: Exactly-once time and persistence
playRequirements.behaviour: Save committed state and guard worker replies, time batches and cross-tab editing ownership.

playRequirements.title: Bounded long-play histories
playRequirements.behaviour: Replace the portfolio hard-stop at 2,000 journal entries with bounded history and durable summaries/checkpoints.

playRequirements.title: Static build and usable deployment path
playRequirements.behaviour: Keep the browser-only static build and existing internationalisation/offline structure.

playRequirements.title: Source and requirement accounting
playRequirements.behaviour: Preserve immutable source packs, MIT notices, history, stable mapping IDs and outstanding obligations.

playRequirements.title: Visible-UI commercial journeys
playRequirements.behaviour: Exercise real controls on the actual candidate build, not only DOM strings or direct dispatch.

playRequirements.title: Behavioural regression and gates
playRequirements.behaviour: Run the existing verification ladder on the changed behaviours and declared candidate.

playRequirements.title: Human pilot and honest handoff
playRequirements.behaviour: Prepare an exploratory upstream/port comparison and report implementation evidence separately from human evidence.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Provider business and home market
mechanics.fidelityRule: Home market affects available supply and customers; it is not a legal approval.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Customer site or provider service hub
mechanics.fidelityRule: Keep tenant, customer, site and shared provider hub distinct.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: UC/CC platform, gateway and media capacity
mechanics.fidelityRule: Transport bandwidth, voice sessions, named seats and agents remain different.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Carrier, PSTN and wholesale communications supply
mechanics.fidelityRule: A carrier connection does not automatically supply a CC workforce.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Supported federation, interoperability and shared connectivity
mechanics.fidelityRule: Do not imply that UC federation works like universal free internet peering.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Direct routing, SBC or dedicated interconnect/integration
mechanics.fidelityRule: Protocol/media/authority requirements are explicit; a drawn line grants nothing.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Site connectivity, carrier paths and deployment projects
mechanics.fidelityRule: Retain literal transport where it affects UC; integration links are a separate edge type.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Retained underlay and typed session/media upgrades
mechanics.fidelityRule: Never translate every Gbit/s into a seat count.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Local media, local information processing or reusable work
mechanics.fidelityRule: Mapping is conditional: each source cache obligation needs a causal counterpart, not a forced noun swap.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Recurring managed UC users and small-business contracts
mechanics.fidelityRule: Opening customers have authored requirements and activation conditions.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: UC, CC, video and managed-service opportunities
mechanics.fidelityRule: Accepted offer, deployed capacity, service delivery and earned revenue are separate.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Customer jobs, session occupancy, queues and backlogs
mechanics.fidelityRule: One customer case can cross channels; avoid double-counting resolution.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Reachable people, numbers, tenants, channels and supported joins
mechanics.fidelityRule: A global health score cannot replace a specific reachability or policy failure.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Experience, contract confidence and renewal
mechanics.fidelityRule: Use period history and segment needs, not a final readiness flag.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Service incidents and funded recovery
mechanics.fidelityRule: Incident scheduling belongs to the scenario. Repair completes only after work.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Synthetic abuse, admission, fraud and resilience choices
mechanics.fidelityRule: Retain distinctions between capacity attack, account abuse and media failure.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Provider treasury, credit and lease/buy decisions
mechanics.fidelityRule: Loan proceeds are financing, not operating profit.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Provider margin, cash, commitments and delivered workload
mechanics.fidelityRule: Use fictional cents and declared /period units; separate diagnostic totals.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Commercial capabilities and meaningful expansion
mechanics.fidelityRule: A badge without a new choice is supplementary, not sufficient progression.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Partner offers, qualification, integration and training opportunities
mechanics.fidelityRule: Give every event a cost or opportunity tradeoff; no mandatory networking busywork.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Provisioning, assurance and lifecycle automation
mechanics.fidelityRule: Automation changes work economics; it does not bypass authority or guarantee outcomes.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Bundles, vendor-direct offers, channel shifts and lifecycle changes
mechanics.fidelityRule: A small authored market is enough; every actor need not be an autonomous AI corporation.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Segment missions and seeded contract challenges
mechanics.fidelityRule: Declare scenario fiction and do not turn jurisdiction labels into certification.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Shared provider clock
mechanics.fidelityRule: Frame rate, visual particles and hidden-tab time do not change business rules.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Customer/service inspector and interaction replay
mechanics.fidelityRule: Raw evidence remains available as a diagnostic drilldown.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Migration, retirement and service-policy planning
mechanics.fidelityRule: Keep active work, authority, data retention and rollback conditions explicit.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Fictional UC/CC suppliers, partners, customers and competitors
mechanics.fidelityRule: Keep all source IDs. Similar economics may share code; source-specific behaviour remains separately evidenced.

mechanics.ucCcReplacement: Workforce, journeys, CPaaS, information and boundary systems
mechanics.fidelityRule: Do not present the 94 additions as 94 compulsory setup tasks.

goals.name: First customer live
goals.sourceRole: Open your home city and press “Launch broadband”. Eyeballs are people at home watching cat videos. They pay you every month.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: External calling operational
goals.sourceRole: Your eyeballs want everything. Buy IP transit from a Tier 1 or Tier 2 in your city. Transit gives you the full routing table.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: First ecosystem integration
goals.sourceRole: Get a port at an IX: a big shared switch where networks swap traffic for free instead of paying transit.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Five working partner services
goals.sourceRole: On the Peering tab, request sessions, or join the route server to peer with every open network at once.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Second site connected
goals.sourceRole: Drag from your pink router to another city. Short hops are cheap. Oceans are not.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: First managed business contract
goals.sourceRole: Businesses show up with a $ bubble. You need a POP in their city. Check the Deals tab.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Continuity proven
goals.sourceRole: Things break all the time. Build a second path or a second upstream so traffic reroutes when something dies.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Local media or speech service
goals.sourceRole: Big CDNs give you free cache boxes once you send them enough traffic. Free bandwidth, just add power.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Dedicated carrier interconnect
goals.sourceRole: A private cross-connect to one network in the same data center, for when traffic outgrows the IX.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Communications abuse defences
goals.sourceRole: Build a scrubbing center from a POP's Infra tab. It cleans attacks up to its capacity and lets you sell DDoS protection.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Three-region service footprint
goals.sourceRole: Have POPs on 3 continents. Subsea cables cost a fortune, so plan the route.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Established communications MSP
goals.sourceRole: 5+ POPs, ports on 3+ IXs and 15+ peering sessions.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: First sustained service scale target
goals.sourceRole: A terabit per second of happy traffic.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Own service infrastructure
goals.sourceRole: Lease or dig dark fiber, put a DWDM system on it and light a channel. Cheaper per bit than waves, once it works.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Independent operating sites
goals.sourceRole: Add a second site in a metro from the Infra tab, so one power cut no longer takes the whole city dark.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Five-region portfolio
goals.sourceRole: POPs in five of the six regions on the map.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Major enterprise or public-service contract
goals.sourceRole: Land an AI WAN, a multi-site training run or a fiber-pairs deal with a hyperscaler. Customer level 4 and a POP near their campus required.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: High-volume customer-service target
goals.sourceRole: Ten terabits per second of happy traffic. The giants will notice.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

goals.name: Sustainable ecosystem operator
goals.sourceRole: Peer with every Tier 1 over PNIs and cancel every transit port. Then nobody charges you to reach the internet.
goals.contextualHome: Provider goals, service milestones and operational evidence

globalCaveat: Statuses describe current implementation coverage visible in this checkout, not canonical source dispositions. The new diagnostic rows are bounded evidence, not source-fidelity completion. No status is full fidelity unless specifically proven by its own source-specific behaviour; this accounting makes no disposition changes.

obligationCatalog.action: ACTION-REVIEW: Compare this source action with its provider-contextual home and dispatch semantics; retain an explicit Lab disposition where appropriate. Handler presence alone is not adaptation.
obligationCatalog.actor: ACTOR-REVIEW: A profile or ID reference is not gameplay. Provide at least one evidenced action, economic/dependency/capacity consequence, failure or customer outcome, with authority and support roles explicit.
obligationCatalog.view: VIEW-REVIEW: Confirm the named purpose in current provider UI, stable through ticks, keyboard reachable, mobile usable, and evidenced in the current browser candidate.
obligationCatalog.tutorial: TUTORIAL-REVIEW: Implement the exact adapted step in the provider six-step flow, with state-aware progress, resume and skip; legacy training retention is separate.
obligationCatalog.progress: PROGRESSION-REVIEW: Map the exact source predicate, resulting unlock and reward; generic progression infrastructure is not source fidelity.
obligationCatalog.mechanic: MECHANIC-REVIEW: Verify source-specific behaviour and consequences through a distinct acceptance case; shared generic recipes do not close this obligation.
obligationCatalog.play: PLAY-REVIEW: Complete each listed acceptance point through integrated engine/UI/worker/save/browser surfaces as applicable; the source requirement is authoritative.
